extracted.intended_audience: EU companies (large undertakings, listed SMEs, non-EU parents), corporate sustainability/reporting officers, finance, audit and compliance teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for companies required to prepare sustainability (ESG) reports under the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), including scope, reporting topics, standards (ESRS), assurance, timelines and implementation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: companies subject to the CSRD
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSRD sets out four groups of affected companies: Companies already subject to the NFRD; All large companies (two of three criteria met): >250 employees and/or >EUR40M turnover and/or >EUR20M total assets; Listed SMEs (except micro-undertakings); Companies with non-EU parent companies with a combined group turnover in the EU of >EUR150M for 2 consecutive years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMEs have the option to opt out for two years (reporting in 2029 on 2028 data). Micro-undertakings are defined as companies that do not exceed two of the following three criteria (including subsidiaries): 10 employees, net revenue of EUR 700,000 or total assets of EUR 350,000. Separate standards will be developed for SMEs and non-EU parent companies (to be adopted by 30 June 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting topics: environmental, social and governance (topic-specific disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are to report on: Environmental protection; Social responsibility and treatment of employees; Respect for human rights; Anti-corruption and bribery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic-specific disclosures include: Environmental (including EU Taxonomy), Social, Governance, and Sector-specific standards. Reporting will cover E, S & G (not limited to climate-only).

rubrics_metrics.name: General disclosures (business model, strategy, governance, KPIs and targets, diversity, risk management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must disclose general information such as business model, strategy and policies; KPIs and targets (forward-looking information); company and sustainability governance; double materiality assessment and due diligence; diversity on company boards; risk and opportunity management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information should contain forward-looking and retrospective information. KPIs and targets should be linked to strategy, risks & opportunities and actions. Disclosures must enable stakeholders to evaluate non-financial performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting standards to use: binding ESRS (European Sustainability Reporting Standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting is to be in accordance with binding European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) to be developed by EFRAG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While current practices referenced recognized national, Union-based or international frameworks, CSRD introduces binding ESRS. Separate ESRS-based standards for SMEs and non-EU parent companies are to be developed/adopted by set dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double materiality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must perform a double materiality assessment identifying (a) the undertaking’s impacts on society and the environment (impact materiality) and (b) how sustainability matters affect the undertaking (financial materiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double materiality increases complexity by requiring consideration of both impact and financial channels, and requires assessing the whole value chain. It affects topic selection, KPIs and disclosures and requires both forward-looking and retrospective information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets and progress reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSRD requires organizations to set targets related to sustainability matters and report progress towards these targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets should be clear per material topic, linked to strategy, and accompanied by KPI identification and performance measurement. Forward-looking information is expected alongside retrospective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent third-party assurance (assurance readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD foresees independent mandatory assurance on reported information, including compliance with ESRS — mandatory limited level of assurance expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance may include integration in the Auditor’s Report, involvement of the key audit partner, and scope to include EU Taxonomy. Companies must 'get ready to be audited' as annual assurance obligations apply. Under previous NFRD regimes assurance was non-mandatory in many countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to report: inclusion in the Management Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainability information is to be included in the Management Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory inclusion in the Management Report may require reshaping existing report structure to accommodate new and different types of information. (Previously some jurisdictions allowed a separate report.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and filing: electronic/machine-readable submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported information must be submitted in electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically companies used online or PDF versions; CSRD requires electronic submission (machine-readable formats) to support comparability and stakeholder use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased timeline for reporting (cohort-specific start dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting obligations are phased: reporting entities already subject to NFRD should start gathering 2024 data to report in 2025; large reporting entities not currently subject to NFRD should start gathering 2025 data to report in 2026; listed SMEs, small and non-complex credit institutions and captive insurers should start gathering 2026 data to report in 2027 (SME opt-out applies); companies with non-EU parent companies should start gathering 2028 data to report in 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First and second sets of ESRS will be adopted by the EU Commission in 2024/2025 (including sector-specific standards). Companies must plan preparatory work early to ensure timely compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with TCFD and climate objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies shall disclose information in line with the TCFD, the transition to a sustainable economy, with limiting global warming to 1.5°C and with climate neutrality by 2050.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSRD alignment with TCFD-style reporting implies scenario analysis, transition planning and climate-related risk disclosure. CSRD covers E, S & G, and is broader than climate-only frameworks (e.g., SEC, ISSB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkage to the European Taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRS will require disclosure of information aligned with the European Taxonomy for companies in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxonomy alignment may be part of the assurance scope and of KPI disclosures; reporting should include Taxonomy-relevant metrics and processes used to identify relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data readiness assessment and systems/IT architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform data readiness assessments per topic or KPI through the lens of governance, processes & controls and systems; design system architecture for ESG data management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional criteria identification, assistance in choosing/configuring ESG reporting IT solutions with vendors, designing KPI dashboards and consolidation methodology are recommended. Reporting will require increased data collection across value chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: KPI identification, calculation and narrative (reporting manual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify KPIs per material topic; define KPI calculation methods and narrative. Examples: GHG emissions, EU Taxonomy metrics, metrics for material biodiversity-related impacts, resource in-/outflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a reporting manual with KPI definitions, calculation formulas, scope and reporting boundaries to ensure consistency and auditability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating model, roles, controls and governance for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Design reporting-related processes, role overlays, position-to-role mapping, policies and non-financial controls as part of target operating model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess current operating model maturity; map responsibilities for ESG reporting and embed controls to ensure data quality, evidence trails and audit readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, change management and group-wide implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement tailored training plans across ESG for target audiences across the whole group, and deploy systems and processes group-wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should cover awareness to action; change management supports adoption of new reporting processes. Group-wide implementation includes system deployment and assurance readiness activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical implementation approach (KPMG five-phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: A five-phases approach to embed CSRD requirements: Phase 1 Impact assessment; Phase 2 Define materiality; Phase 3 Assess maturity; Phase 4 Design ESG reporting setup; Phase 5 Group-wide implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each phase contains specific sub-activities (e.g., 1.1 Regulatory radar, 2.1 Double materiality, 3.1 Gap assessment, 4.2 KPI calculation & narrative, 5.3 Assurance readiness). The approach is modular and adaptable to company circumstances.
